title: Charlie Parker leaves; John Jackson takes the first alto chair
summary: Restless Parker quits before he starts causing trouble and recommends his schoolmate John Jackson.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: So by this time, the band was pretty well launched. Incidentally, Charlie Parker had left the band just before that date. Because Charlie was a restless kind of a person. He didn't care to be bottled up too long any place. So he really went to Billy and told him that he was going to leave the band, because he felt like if he didn't he would start screwing up, and he didn't want to do that. When working with the band he was pretty much on good behavior at all times. There were times when we would start playing at 9 o'clock, and Charlie would come in at maybe 10:30 or 11, but that didn't

happen too often. So he decided he would leave the band. That's when he sent for and got an old school-mate of his, a fellow that he'd grown up with and had played in Jay McShann's band with him, a fellow named John Jackson, a very good saxophone player. John was a quiet sort of a fellow, and I think labored in the shadow of Charlie Parker. He always felt a little inferior to Charlie, and he was a little insecure about what he was doing. But everybody loved the way John played, and he was a very good first alto saxophone player. And he remained with the band quite a while.
